title: Impact of continuing folic acid after the first trimester of pregnancy: findings of a randomized trial of Folic Acid Supplementation in the Second and Third Trimesters
authors: McNulty B, McNulty H, Marshall B, Ward M, Molloy AM, Scott JM, et al.
population: Pregnant women aged 18 to 35 years with singleton uncomplicated pregnancies in Northern Ireland who had taken folic acid in the first trimester, randomised at the start of trimester 2 to continue 400 µg/day or to stop with placebo
funder: Supported by the Northern Ireland Department for Employment and Learning (PhD funding to B McNulty).
result: Results read from the published abstract. 119 women completed (59 folic acid, 60 placebo). In women who stopped, serum folate fell from 45.7 ± 21.3 to 19.5 ± 16.5 nmol/L between gestational weeks 14 and 36 and homocysteine rose from 6.6 ± 2.3 to 7.6 ± 2.3 µmol/L; continuation prevented these changes and raised red cell folate from 1203 ± 639 to 1746 ± 683 nmol/L. Cord red cell folate 1993 ± 862 against 1418 ± 557 nmol/L (P = 0.001). The authors state that benefits for pregnancy outcomes or early childhood require additional study.
